groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
W: So, I've been thinking, this summer, instead of our usual holiday rental, I'd like to try renting a camper van and exploring a bit more.
M: A camper van? You mean to spend the summer living out of a car?
W: Yes, a camper van. And no, it's nothing like living out of a car. These are proper vans with full-size beds to sleep in. Some even have kitchens. This way, we wouldn't have to be locked into one place during our holiday. We'd be able to visit so many more places and travel at our own pace. The rates of most hotels and holiday homes really soar in the summer anyway. We'd probably save a lot of money as well.
M: I think my grandfather had a van like that. It doesn't sound that appealing to me.
W: Today's camper vans are completely different. These days, they're equipped with all the modern comforts. I've seen quite a few with solar panels that provide electricity for when you're stopped. This way, you can still use your computer or charge your phone. And most even have Wi-Fi, so if the weather's not great, you could stream videos.
M: I'm warming up to the idea. Keep talking.
W: Loads of people are committing to this trend full time. Check it out online. Lots of people stream videos of their alternative lifestyles and actually earn a salary. Imagine having that kind of freedom to go anywhere you want and work from anywhere in the world.
M: Okay, we can consider it. As long as the basic needs like toilet and showers are covered, I'm definitely in. Do you think there will be enough room for my mountain bike? What about food delivery? Will we be able to order at the van? Will there be enough space for the dog? We wouldn't want to leave him behind.
W: Slow down. Glad you're excited about it. Let's start by looking at what's available first.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
W: You wanted to see me?
M: Yes, I'll get straight to the point. Over the past month or so, it has become apparent that your performance has dipped. You've been late to work several times these past few weeks, which is very uncharacteristic of you. But what really concerns me is your curtailed output. Lately, you seem to be constantly one step behind. What's going on?
W: I'm sorry. I'm going through some unfortunate family issues at the moment. It's a personal matter, so if you don't mind, I much prefer we don't get into it. Nevertheless, I expect it to have all blown over in another month or so.
M: Do you need some time off?
W: Actually, yes. Would it be possible to take the next two Mondays off? I was deliberating whether I should ask for this, but now that we're here…
M: Sure thing. But if you needed some leave, why didn't you ask for it earlier?
W: I'm not sure why. I guess I kind of felt bad asking for it.
M: You shouldn't feel bad asking for leave, especially if you need it.
W: I know. You're right. I'm sorry.
M: Look, you've been with us almost five years and I personally really value your proficiency at your job. It makes my job far easier. In addition, I can assure you that management as a whole also holds you in high regard.
W: Thank you.
M: What I need is for you to be back at your 100%. Are you sure taking two Mondays off will suffice?
W: It'll be enough. I'm sure of it.
M: Okay, good. So this is what we're going to do. You will take those days off, and I expect that you will gradually come back to your usual self. Then in two months' time, we will catch up again to see how you are faring.
W: Sounds good. Thank you for your understanding.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material: There are many factors that impact our health. These include our finances, our emotions and the way we work. Education is one such factor. Research suggests that higher levels of education can lead to better health and even greater longevity. But what about the education of your partner? New research seeks to answer this question. Researchers use data from a longitudinal study. The data came from surveys first administered to high school seniors in 1957. The surveys ended in 2011. The team found that a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health. This remained the case when adjusting for other factors, such as participants' own education, social background and health status before and after marriage. The authors suggest that high levels of education provide shared social, intellectual, emotional and financial resources. These include things like higher levels of emotional intelligence, particular skills or knowledge, or more money. The researchers concede that an individual's own level of education is clearly important for their health, but they assert that individuals also can reap the benefits of their partner's education. It is noteworthy that the effects vary by gender. For women, health was more closely correlated to their spouse's education than for men. The team suggests this may be related to the time period of the study. Women in this sample had lower levels of education and lower occupational achievements than the men. The researchers' hypothesis is that this made the husband's resources more likely to have a shared impact.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material: Climate scientists predict that many parts of the world will be increasingly prone to floods. This is a serious risk to human lives and property. So understanding and accurately forecasting flood risks is a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe. In 2017, Derek Loftis of the Virginia Institute of Marine Science started a project called Catch the King. It uses a smartphone app to collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides. He'll use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model, called TideWatch. Loftis's mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there. But collecting necessary data and then processing that information quickly enough to make usable forecasts is anything but easy. Accurate flood forecasts require an understanding of the situation on the ground. By the early 2000s, supercomputing had advanced enough that scientists could integrate weather forecasting models with such measurements. But they still didn't have the critically important ability to forecast fast-moving floods in real time. So, in 2017, Loftis and colleagues set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors throughout the flood risk community of Norfolk, Virginia. The new sensors relayed rough measurements about water height and movement to a computer at the Virginia Institute. Along with those sensors, hundreds of local citizens take photos of rising tides and transmit them in real time to the institute. Scientists hope that the data collected by these citizens can help sharpen the ability to forecast exactly when and where damaging floods will occur.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Now, it's become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree, but as Current Population Survey data show, there has been a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees compared with those who have them. This decline began in the 1960s and has become more serious over time.
What has actually caused this decline? Well, economists have been working to ascertain the roots of the decline for decades and have come up with several theories. One popular theory is that it's a case of too low wages for jobs that don't require a degree. An alternate theory is that there were more jobs not requiring a college degree in the past than now.
A recent working paper from the National Bureau of Economic Research reviewed those theories and put forward additional hypotheses about the causes of the problem. Let's look at that paper now. First, the researchers considered the issue of wages. As the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without, economists have suggested that men aren't as interested in taking some of the less lucrative jobs. While the authors of the paper found truth in this explanation, they assert that low wages can't be the only factor, as wages for men without college degrees, adjusting for inflation, haven't changed much since the 1960s, making it hard to see why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages.
This leads to the second theory, that more jobs require a college degree today than in the past. Indeed, that theory seems valid, because in America today, 2/3 of jobs are filled by workers with at least some college education. However, the authors of the paper argue that there are other factors amplifying the problem.
They identified two new potential explanations: the first being the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees since the 1960s; and the second being the increase in women participating in the workforce that was concurrent with the decline in marriage. These two changes mean that men might not have families to support, or if they do, their wives might be doing more of the providing, both of which might remove the financial incentive to work. The authors of the paper concede that research on the subject isn't complete, but they argue that their work supports the value of a college education.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
While an increasing number of people are trying to eat less meat, a market research team has found in its latest fashion and sustainability report that the trend is now spreading from kitchen to closet. It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes, with 42% saying it was important to them. The researchers of the team predicted that the next year would see a boom in animal-free shoe collections, since they heard shoppers of all ages say they would buy footwear designated as "vegan", meaning the goods were produced without using any animal or animal part.
As well as being on trend, and with a much better ring to it than synthetic leather, the vegan label does convey an important extra distinction. If you label something as vegan, then the whole product needs to be animal free. That means checking things like the glue that holds the shoe together, for example, and the chemicals used for finishing them. At the top end, some of the world-renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time. In fact, some of the companies are now exploring a leather substitute and a silk replacement made from mushrooms.
The Animal Free Product Society says they've seen a boom in products registered with the vegan trademark. In 2018, there were 119. So far this year, it says an unprecedented 1,956 have been registered. New products are being added daily. There are fur coats that are vegan, plastic vegan belts and shoes made from tree bark or natural rubber labelled vegan. These new products aren't coming at an extra cost to consumers though. Vegan boots cost the same as the leather originals. New Look, one of the first reputable store chains to use the vegan trademark, prices ballet shoes at £7.99 and a vegan laptop handbag at £29.99, comparable with its other products.
This signifies a change. In the past, ethical products, whether they were fair trade or organic, came at a premium. However, it is unclear whether these new products can be considered ethical. The debate over durability, crop-growing impacts, pollution and recyclability is a complicated one, not to mention the ethics around the working conditions for people making the products, whatever the component materials. Environmental campaigners advise that the best approach is to buy less, never mind what the item is made of.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
By the end of 2016, anyone who had been paying even passing attention to the news headlines was highly likely to conclude that everything was terrible, and that the world was going to hell. It was easy to feel depressed by the wars in different parts of the world, the spread of deadly viruses or terror attacks.
Yet, 2016 was the best year in the history of humanity. Child mortality was roughly half what it was as recently as 1990. And 300,000 more people gained access to electricity each day. Every single measure of material and environmental welfare in America, Europe, Asia, Africa and the world as a whole has improved rather than deteriorated. We are living in history's most peaceful era, with violence of all kinds in steep decline. Those are the facts. So why aren't we all optimists?
In a 2015 survey for YouGov, 65% of British people and 81% of the French said they thought the world was getting worse. However, according to numerous sensible statistics, these people are simply wrong. Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century. Yet people do. Why?
Our prevailing mood of despair is irrational. It says more about us than it does about how things really are. It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors—but now, in a media-saturated era, constantly mislead us. Once upon a time, it was of great survival value to be worried about everything that could go wrong. This is what makes bad news especially compelling.
In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival. The caveman who always assumed there was a lion behind the next rock would usually be wrong, but he'd be much more likely to survive and reproduce than one who always assumed the opposite. But that was all before newspapers, television and the internet. In today's hyper connected times, our addiction to bad news just leads us to vacuum up depressing or enraging stories from across the globe. Whether these news stories threaten us or not, we conclude that things are much worse than they actually are. Really good news, on the other hand, can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper because predictable daily events by definition aren't news.

questions.prompt: What has the woman been thinking of doing for this summer?
options: Renting a car instead of driving their own.
Surfing online to check out the best deals.
Exploring more summer holiday resorts.
Spending their holidays in a novel way.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What has the woman been thinking of doing for this summer? 

 【翻译】 这位女士一直在考虑今年夏天做什么? 
 A)  租一辆车而不是开他们自己的车。 
 B)  在网上浏览以查看最优惠的价格。 
 C)  探索更多的避暑度假胜地。 
 D)  以一种新颖的方式度过假期。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Spending their holidays in a novel way. 
 【定位】 P1 So, I've been thinking, this summer, instead of our usual holiday rental, I'd like to try renting a camper van and exploring a bit more. 
 嗯，我一直在想，今年夏天，不走我们往常租度假屋那一套，我想试试租一辆房车、多走走看看。 

 【信号】 意愿句I'd like to 。答案信号是女方直接表达意愿的 I'd like to try renting a camper van and exploring a bit more，I'd like to（我想）这类意愿句正是“她想做什么”的落点，紧跟在 I've been thinking 之后，开门见山。 

 【替换】 renting a camper van and exploring a bit more ↔ Spending their holidays in a novel way 具体做法概括为“新方式” 
 instead of our usual holiday rental ↔ in a novel way “不走老一套”=“新方式” 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项 Renting a car instead of driving their own. 盗用了原文 renting a camper van 里的 renting，听到“租”就想选；但她租的是 camper van（房车）不是普通 car，更没说“不开自己的车”，是把原词嫁接到一个原文没有的意思上。  借用原文：renting a camper van 

 B) 原词陷阱 Surfing online to check out the best deals. 里 online 确实在录音里出现过，但那是后文 Check it out online 让对方上网看这种生活方式，并非她“这个夏天想做的事”，时间点和意图都错位。  借用原文：Check it out online 

 C) 偷换概念 Exploring more summer holiday resorts. 借用了 exploring 和 summer holiday 的字眼，听感很熟；但她说的是 exploring a bit more（多走走看看更多地方），从没提“度假胜地 resorts”，是把模糊的“多探索”偷换成具体的“逛度假村”。  借用原文：exploring a bit more

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the man's grandfather from the conversation?
options: He once owned a van.
He was well travelled.
He did not find holiday homes appealing.
He did not like to be locked into one place.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the man's grandfather from the conversation? 

 【翻译】 从对话中我们了解到这位男士的祖父有什么情况? 
 A)  他曾经拥有一辆面包车。 
 B)  他去过很多地方旅行。 
 C)  他觉得度假屋没有吸引力。 
 D)  他不喜欢被限制在一个地方。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） He once owned a van. 
 【定位】 P4 M: I think my grandfather had a van like that. It doesn't sound that appealing to me. 
 男：我记得我爷爷有过一辆那样的车。这听着对我没什么吸引力。 

 【信号】 提到祖父那一句 。答案信号就是男方亲口提到祖父的 I think my grandfather had a van like that——题目点名 grandfather，原文唯一讲祖父的就是这句，had a van 直接给出关于祖父的事实。 

 【替换】 my grandfather had a van like that ↔ He once owned a van had a van=owned a van 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 He was well travelled.（他见多识广 / 走过很多地方）原文从未说祖父，是无中生有；对话只说祖父有过车，没说他爱旅行，属未提及的凭空拔高。 
 C) 张冠李戴 He did not find holiday homes appealing. 盗用了原文 It doesn't sound that appealing to me 里的 appealing；但说“不吸引人”的是男方本人对房车主意的反应，且嫌的是房车不是 holiday homes，把男方的话张冠李戴成祖父的态度。  借用原文：It doesn't sound that appealing to me 

 D) 张冠李戴 He did not like to be locked into one place. 盗用了 we wouldn't have to be locked into one place 的 locked into one place；但那是女方在讲房车的好处，主语是“我们”，不是祖父的喜好，人物与语境双重错位。  借用原文：we wouldn't have to be locked into one place

questions.prompt: What can many camper vans do nowadays according to the woman?
options: Ensure the safety of passengers.
Drive under any weather condition.
Receive instructions via computers.
Generate their own electricity.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What can many camper vans do nowadays according to the woman? 

 【翻译】 根据这位女士的说法,现在许多露营车能做什么? 
 A)  确保乘客的安全。 
 B)  在任何天气条件下行驶。 
 C)  通过计算机接收指令。 
 D)  自行发电。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Generate their own electricity. 
 【定位】 P5 I've seen quite a few with solar panels that provide electricity for when you're stopped. 
 我见过不少装了太阳能板的，停车时能供电。 

 【信号】 功能描述provide electricity 。答案信号是描述具体功能的 solar panels that provide electricity——provide electricity（提供电力）直接说出房车“能做什么”，是这段功能罗列里与选项对得上的那一句。 

 【替换】 solar panels that provide electricity ↔ Generate their own electricity 供电=自己发电 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Ensure the safety of passengers. 原文整段讲的是供电、Wi-Fi、看视频这些舒适功能，从未提“保障乘客安全”，是凭常识硬加的功能，属未提及。 
 B) 原词陷阱 Drive under any weather condition. 利用了原文 if the weather's not great 的 weather；但原文说的是“天气不好时可以看流媒体视频”，是娱乐功能，根本不是“任何天气都能开车”，把 weather 嫁接到一个原文没有的能力上。  借用原文：if the weather's not great 

 C) 原词陷阱 Receive instructions via computers. 盗用了原文 you can still use your computer 里的 computer；但原文是“你可以用自己的电脑”，主语是人在用电脑，不是房车“通过电脑接收指令”，把人的行为偷换成车的功能。  借用原文：you can still use your computer

questions.prompt: What idea does the woman find attractive?
options: Having one's basic needs covered while away from home.
Enjoying the freedom to choose where to go and work.
Slowing down in one's increasingly hectic life.
Riding one's mountain bike on vacation.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What idea does the woman find attractive? 

 【翻译】 这位女士觉得什么想法有吸引力? 
 A)  离家在外时基本需求得到满足。 
 B)  享有选择去哪里和在哪里工作的自由。 
 C)  在日益忙碌的生活中放慢节奏。 
 D)  度假时骑山地自行车。 

 【答案】 B （态度观点题） Enjoying the freedom to choose where to go and work. 
 【定位】 P7 Imagine having that kind of freedom to go anywhere you want and work from anywhere in the world. 
 想象一下，拥有那种自由——想去哪儿就去哪儿，还能在世界任何地方工作。 

 【信号】 向往句Imagine having 。答案信号是女方满怀憧憬的 Imagine having that kind of freedom——Imagine having（想象一下拥有）是她表达向往的语气，紧跟其后的 freedom 就是她觉得吸引人的那一点。 

 【替换】 that kind of freedom to go anywhere you want and work from anywhere in the world ↔ Enjoying the freedom to choose where to go and work 几乎逐点对应的同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 Having one's basic needs covered while away from home. 盗用了原文 the basic needs like toilet and showers are covered；但说在意 basic needs 的是男方（M），不是女方，题目问的是女方觉得什么吸引人，人物错位。  借用原文：the basic needs like toilet and showers are covered 

 C) 偷换概念 Slowing down in one's increasingly hectic life. 借用了原文 Slow down 里的 slow down；但那是女方让激动的男方“别急、慢点说”，是对话节奏用语，根本不是她觉得吸引人的生活理念，把口语提醒偷换成人生主张。  借用原文：Slow down 

 D) 张冠李戴 Riding one's mountain bike on vacation. 盗用了原文 my mountain bike；但提山地车的是男方（担心装不装得下），与女方“觉得吸引人”毫无关系，人物和语境都错。  借用原文：my mountain bike

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the woman from the man's description?
options: She has missed several important appointments lately.
Her job performance has worsened over the past month.
She has lagged behind most of her co-workers in output.
Her physical health has deteriorated these past few weeks.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the woman from the man's description? 

 【翻译】 从男士的描述中我们对这位女士了解到什么? 
 A)  她最近错过了几个重要的约会。 
 B)  她过去一个月的工作表现变差了。 
 C)  她的产出落后于大多数同事。 
 D)  她过去几周的身体健康状况恶化了。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Her job performance has worsened over the past month. 
 【定位】 P2 Over the past month or so, it has become apparent that your performance has dipped. You've been late to work several times these past few weeks, which is very uncharacteristic of you. But what really concerns me is your curtailed output. 
 在过去一个月左右，很明显你的表现下滑了。这几周你好几次上班迟到，这很不像你。但真正让我担心的是你产出减少了。 

 【信号】 总起定性句 + 转折强调 。男方开口就给总定性 your performance has dipped，又用 But what really concerns me 的转折把重点压到"产出减少"上；"总起判断句 + But 后的强调"正是答案句信号。 

 【替换】 your performance has dipped ↔ Her job performance has worsened dipped=worsened 同义替换 
 Over the past month or so ↔ over the past month 时间范围对应 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 原文确说她 late to work several times（多次迟到），A 却说 missed several important appointments（错过重要约会），盗用"several"和"迟到"的影子，把"上班迟到"偷换成"错过约会"，answer非所答。  借用原文：You've been late to work several times these past few weeks 

 C) 原词陷阱 原文只说她 curtailed output（产出减少），C 用了"output"原词，却擅自加上 lagged behind most of her co-workers（落后于大多数同事），原文从没拿她和同事作比较，属无中生有的范围扩大。  借用原文：what really concerns me is your curtailed output 

 D) 未提及 原文谈的是工作"表现/产出"下滑，D 却说 physical health has deteriorated（身体健康变差），原文男方描述中根本没提她身体生病，属未提及；这与第6题的健康选项呼应，是跨题混淆。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she's experiencing at the moment?
options: Serious health issues.
Disturbance of her mind.
Some problems at home.
Penalty for curtailed output.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say she's experiencing at the moment? 

 【翻译】 女士说她目前正在经历什么? 
 A)  严重的健康问题。 
 B)  精神上的困扰。 
 C)  家里的一些问题。 
 D)  因产出减少而受到的处罚。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Some problems at home. 
 【定位】 P3 I'm sorry. I'm going through some unfortunate family issues at the moment. It's a personal matter, so if you don't mind, I much prefer we don't get into it. 
 对不起，我目前正经历一些不幸的家庭问题。这是私人的事，如果你不介意，我更希望我们不要深谈。 

 【信号】 被问者应答 + I'm going through 自述 。男方追问 What's going on? 后，女方的直接应答 I'm going through some unfortunate family issues 就是答案句；"被问者应答"加上 I'm going through 这种亲口陈述原因的句式，是双重定位信号。 

 【替换】 family issues ↔ problems at home family issues=problems at home 同义替换 
 at the moment ↔ Some "some...issues"对"Some problems" 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 女方从没说自己有 serious health issues（严重健康问题），健康话题是借第5题 D 项的余味来混淆，原文她给的原因是家事不是身体，属未提及。 
 B) 过度推断 Disturbance of her mind（心神不宁）原文从未出现，可能由"她状态不好"脑补出"心理问题"，但女方明说是 family issues、a personal matter，是家事而非精神疾患，属过度推断。 
 D) 原词陷阱 D 的 curtailed output 是从男方第2段 curtailed output 原封搬来的原词，但本题问她"在经历什么"，curtailed output 是"表现"不是"原因"，且"Penalty for"（因…受罚）原文根本没有，盗原词来答非所问。  借用原文：what really concerns me is your curtailed output

questions.prompt: What does the man say makes his job far easier?
options: The woman's work proficiency.
The woman's whole-hearted support.
His engaging personality.
His management capability.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say makes his job far easier? 

 【翻译】 男士说什么使他的工作轻松得多? 
 A)  女士的工作能力。 
 B)  女士的全心全意支持。 
 C)  他有吸引力的个性。 
 D)  他的管理能力。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） The woman's work proficiency. 
 【定位】 P10 I personally really value your proficiency at your job. It makes my job far easier. 
 我个人非常看重你在工作上的熟练。这让我的工作轻松多了。 

 【信号】 题干同款短语 makes my job easier 。原文 It makes my job far easier 与题干 makes his job far easier 是同一短语，前一句的 your proficiency at your job 就是"It"指代的内容，定位锁这两句。 

 【替换】 your proficiency at your job ↔ The woman's work proficiency your=the woman's，视角转换 

 【排除】 B) 偷换概念 原文男方说 I personally really value your proficiency（看重你的熟练），B 借"value/对她的肯定"的影子说成 whole-hearted support（全心全意的支持），但让他工作轻松的是她的"熟练"不是"支持"，原文没说她全力支持他，属偷换概念。  借用原文：I personally really value your proficiency at your job 

 C) 张冠李戴 His engaging personality（他迷人的性格）讲的是男方自己的特质，但原文让工作轻松的是"你的熟练"即女方，C 把归属从女方错挪到男方，且"魅力"原文从未出现，属张冠李戴。 
 D) 张冠李戴 His management capability（他的管理能力）原文从未提及，且方向反了——让工作轻松的是女方的熟练，不是男方自己的管理力，既张冠李戴又无中生有。

questions.prompt: What agreement have the speakers reached by the end of the conversation?
options: The woman will resume her work in two weeks.
The man will be back at his 100% in a couple of weeks.
The woman will be off work on the next two Mondays.
The man will help the woman get back to her usual self.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What agreement have the speakers reached by the end of the conversation? 

 【翻译】 对话结束时双方达成了什么协议? 
 A)  女士将在两周后恢复工作。 
 B)  男士将在几周内恢复到百分之百的状态。 
 C)  女士接下来两个星期一将休假。 
 D)  男士将帮助女士恢复到她平常的状态。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） The woman will be off work on the next two Mondays. 
 【定位】 P5 W: Would it be possible to take the next two Mondays off? ... M: Sure thing. ... M: So this is what we're going to do. You will take those days off, and I expect that you will gradually come back to your usual self. 
 女：能让我接下来两个周一请假吗？……男：当然可以。……男：那我们就这么办，你把那两天休掉，我希望你慢慢恢复到平时的状态。 

 【信号】 请求—应允—拍板三处合一 。女方提出 take the next two Mondays off，男方 Sure thing 应允，结尾再 So this is what we're going to do. You will take those days off 拍板；"请求被应允并在结尾确认"是约定题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 take the next two Mondays off ↔ be off work on the next two Mondays take...off=be off work 同义替换 
 You will take those days off ↔ The woman will be off work 结尾确认句坐实主语是女方 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说 resume her work in two weeks（两周后复工），但原文女方只是休"两个周一"、并非停工两周后才回来；"two"原词在，时间概念却被偷换，且 in two months 才是再约谈时间，A 张冠时间。  借用原文：take the next two Mondays off 

 B) 张冠李戴 B 说 The man will be back at his 100%，但原文 What I need is for you to be back at your 100% 是男方要求"你（女方）"回到100%，主语该是女方不是男方；盗用 100% 原词却把人安反，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：What I need is for you to be back at your 100% 

 D) 过度推断 D 说 The man will help the woman get back to her usual self，但原文是男方期望"你会慢慢恢复"you will gradually come back to your usual self，是女方自己恢复，并非男方"帮"她；盗 usual self 原词却脑补出"帮助"，属过度推断。  借用原文：you will gradually come back to your usual self

questions.prompt: What does research suggest about a higher level of education?
options: It can have an impact on our moods and emotions.
It can enable us to live a healthier and longer life.
It can improve our financial status significantly.
It can help us achieve better work performance.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does research suggest about a higher level of education? 

 【翻译】 研究表明较高的教育水平会带来什么? 
 A)  它可以影响我们的心境和情绪。 
 B)  它可以使我们过上更健康、更长寿的生活。 
 C)  它可以显著改善我们的经济状况。 
 D)  它可以帮助我们取得更好的工作表现。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It can enable us to live a healthier and longer life. 
 【定位】 P1 Research suggests that higher levels of education can lead to better health and even greater longevity. 
 研究表明，更高的教育水平能带来更好的健康状况，甚至更长的寿命。 

 【信号】 题干原词在原文的复现句 。录音里 Research suggests that higher levels of education 几乎逐字复述了题干 What does research suggest about a higher level of education 的措辞，这种'题干怎么问、原文就怎么开头'的句子就是答案句，紧跟其后的 can lead to better health and even greater longevity 即为结论。 

 【替换】 better health and even greater longevity ↔ live a healthier and longer life 名词换成形容词、同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音开头确实念到 our emotions，但那是在列举'影响健康的诸多因素'时提到的，并非说'教育能影响情绪'。选项 have an impact on our moods and emotions 把这个原词搬来，答的却不是题干问的'教育带来什么'。  借用原文：our finances, our emotions and the way we work 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音里 our finances 同样只是被列为'影响健康的因素'之一，原文从未说'教育能显著改善财务'。选项 improve our financial status significantly 借 finances 这个原词设套，与题干所问无关。  借用原文：our finances, our emotions and the way we work 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音说 the way we work 是影响健康的因素之一，并未说'教育能带来更好的工作表现'。选项 achieve better work performance 用 work 这个原词制造熟悉感，但属无中生有。  借用原文：the way we work

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the finding of the new research?
options: One's health tends to differ before and after marriage.
One's health status is related to one's social background.
The wealthier one's spouse is, the healthier one becomes.
The spouse's level of education can impact one's health.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the finding of the new research? 

 【翻译】 我们从这项新研究的发现中了解到什么? 
 A)  一个人的健康状况在婚前和婚后往往有所不同。 
 B)  一个人的健康状况与其社会背景有关。 
 C)  配偶越富有,一个人就越健康。 
 D)  配偶的教育水平可以影响一个人的健康。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The spouse's level of education can impact one's health. 
 【定位】 P1 The team found that a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health. 
 研究团队发现，配偶受教育水平更高的人，往往报告自己的健康状况更好。 

 【信号】 The team found 引出研究结论 。The team found that 是典型的'结论引导句'，篇章里凡以'研究团队发现……'开头的话，几乎必是某道题的答案句；其后整句就是这项新研究的核心发现。 

 【替换】 a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health ↔ The spouse's level of education can impact one's health '配偶教育高→健康好'概括为'配偶教育影响健康' 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音里 health status before and after marriage 是作者明确列出的'被调整掉的其他因素'之一，意在说'即便排除它结论依然成立'，根本不是研究发现。选项 One's health tends to differ before and after marriage 反把这个被排除项当成结论。  借用原文：adjusting for other factors, such as participants' own education, social background and health status before and after marriage 

 B) 原词陷阱 social background 与上一项一样，是被作者 adjusting for 排除掉的干扰因素，原文没说'健康与社会背景有关'是新发现。选项 One's health status is related to one's social background 把被排除项伪装成结论。  借用原文：adjusting for other factors, such as participants' own education, social background and health status before and after marriage 

 C) 偷换概念 研究讲的是配偶'教育'影响健康，C 却说 The wealthier one's spouse is, the healthier one becomes，把'教育'偷换成'财富'。虽然录音后文提到教育能带来 more money 等资源，但那是教育的衍生好处，原文从未把'配偶越富→本人越健康'立为结论。  借用原文：more money

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about the men in the sample of the new research?
options: They benefited a lot from their career achievements.
They showed interest in their spouse's occupations.
They had much in common with their spouses.
They had more education than their spouses.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about the men in the sample of the new research? 

 【翻译】 文章关于新研究样本中的男性说了什么? 
 A)  他们从自己的职业成就中受益匪浅。 
 B)  他们对配偶的职业表现出兴趣。 
 C)  他们与配偶有很多共同点。 
 D)  他们比配偶受过更多教育。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They had more education than their spouses. 
 【定位】 P1 Women in this sample had lower levels of education and lower occupational achievements than the men. 
 该样本中的女性，其受教育水平和职业成就都低于男性。 

 【信号】 比较句 lower…than the men 反推男性更高 。答案句以女性为主语作比较——Women in this sample had lower levels of education…than the men，说女性教育水平低于男性，等于反过来说男性教育水平高于女性。问 men 的题，答案藏在'拿 women 跟 men 比'的这句里，需做一次方向反推。 

 【替换】 Women in this sample had lower levels of education…than the men ↔ They had more education than their spouses '女低于男'与'男多于女'肯否方向对调、等值 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音 lower occupational achievements 里确有 achievements 一词，但它是用来说女性'职业成就低'的，并没说男性'从事业成就中获益良多'。选项 benefited a lot from their career achievements 借 achievements 设套，且把描述对象错安到'获益'这一原文没有的意思上。  借用原文：lower occupational achievements 

 B) 原词陷阱 录音里与 occupation 沾边的只有 occupational achievements，原文从未说男性'对配偶的职业感兴趣'。选项 showed interest in their spouse's occupations 用 occupations 这个原词凑出一个原文没有的行为。  借用原文：lower occupational achievements 

 C) 与原文相反 原文恰恰在讲男女'教育与职业成就有差距'（女性更低），而 They had much in common with their spouses 说男性'与配偶有很多共同点'，方向正好相反，原文也根本没提共同点。

questions.prompt: What is said to be a key challenge for cities prone to floods?
options: Eliminating their root cause.
Forecasting flood risks accurately.
Identifying the cities' geological features.
Finding out the changing climate patterns.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is said to be a key challenge for cities prone to floods? 

 【翻译】 据说对于易发洪水的城市而言，一个关键挑战是什么? 
 A)  消除洪水的根本原因。 
 B)  准确预测洪水风险。 
 C)  识别城市的地质特征。 
 D)  找出不断变化的气候模式。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Forecasting flood risks accurately. 
 【定位】 P1 So understanding and accurately forecasting flood risks is a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe. 
 因此，理解并准确预报洪水风险，对全球易受灾的城市来说是一项关键挑战。 

 【信号】 原句直接出现 key challenge 。这句直接含题干核心名词 a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe，且前面有 So 引出结论，是明确的答案句信号——题干名词在录音里几乎原样出现的那一句，就是落点。 

 【替换】 accurately forecasting flood risks ↔ Forecasting flood risks accurately 同词换序，意思全等 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Eliminating their root cause 谈"消除洪水的根源"，录音通篇讲的是"理解和预报"风险，从未提到消除根源，属凭常识臆想的方向。 
 C) 答非所问 Identifying the cities' geological features 说挑战是"识别城市地质特征"，录音里 challenge 后面跟的是"预报洪水风险"，根本没提地质特征，方向被岔开。 
 D) 原词陷阱 Finding out the changing climate patterns 借了录音开头 Climate scientists predict 里的 climate 制造熟耳感，但那只是引出背景的"气候科学家预测"，挑战并非"弄清气候模式变化"，是典型听到原词就想选的陷阱。

questions.prompt: For what purpose does Derek Loftis collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides?
options: To validate his hypothesis about the gravity of floods.
To determine the frequency of high tides causing floods.
To improve his mathematical flooding model.
To see the feasibility of his project on flooding.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 For what purpose does Derek Loftis collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides? 

 【翻译】 Derek Loftis在大潮期间收集普通市民的数据是出于什么目的? 
 A)  验证他关于洪水严重程度的假设。 
 B)  确定引发洪水的大潮发生频率。 
 C)  改进他的洪水数学模型。 
 D)  了解他的洪水项目的可行性。 

 【答案】 C （目的题） To improve his mathematical flooding model. 
 【定位】 P1 He'll use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model, called TideWatch. 
 他将用这些数据去验证并改进他那个名为 TideWatch 的数学洪水模型。 

 【信号】 use those data to 引出目的 。这句的 use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model 正是目的信号 use… to…，to 后面的动作就是采集数据的目的，是答案句无疑。 

 【替换】 improve his mathematical flooding model ↔ To improve his mathematical flooding model 几乎原句对应 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 To validate his hypothesis about the gravity of floods 借了录音原词 validate and improve，但录音 validate 的宾语是"数学洪水模型"，不是"关于洪水严重性的假设"——盗了动词、换了宾语。 
 B) 原词陷阱 To determine the frequency of high tides causing floods 盗用 high tides，但录音里 high tides 是"采集数据的时机"，目的并非"测高潮致洪的频率"，把时间状语硬说成目的。 
 D) 未提及 To see the feasibility of his project on flooding 说目的是"看项目可行性"，录音从未提 feasibility 或"看可行性"，纯属添加。

questions.prompt: What does the passage say is Derek Loftis's mission?
options: To study the consequences of high tides on flooded areas.
To teach local citizens how to collect data of incoming floods.
To forecast rapid floods in real time.
To classify the flooding data processed.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say is Derek Loftis's mission? 

 【翻译】 文章说Derek Loftis的使命是什么? 
 A)  研究大潮对洪水淹没地区的后果。 
 B)  教当地市民如何收集即将到来的洪水的数据。 
 C)  实时预报快速洪水。 
 D)  对处理过的洪水数据进行分类。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） To forecast rapid floods in real time. 
 【定位】 P1 Loftis's mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there. ... But they still didn't have the critically important ability to forecast fast-moving floods in real time. 
 Loftis 的使命是：在水流到某处之前，就知道它会去哪里。……但他们仍不具备实时预报快速移动洪水这一至关重要的能力。 

 【信号】 mission is to + 后文同义解释 。信号句 Loftis's mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there 直接点出使命；它较抽象，录音随后用 forecast fast-moving floods in real time 把这一使命具体化，两处合起来锁定答案。 

 【替换】 to know where the water goes before it goes there ↔ To forecast rapid floods in real time 形象说法换成专业说法 
 forecast fast-moving floods in real time ↔ To forecast rapid floods in real time fast-moving=rapid，近义词替换 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 To study the consequences of high tides on flooded areas 借了录音的 high tides，但录音说的使命是"实时预报"，不是"研究高潮对淹没区的后果"，study consequences 是录音没有的动作。 
 B) 张冠李戴 To teach local citizens how to collect data of incoming floods 盗用 citizens、collect data，但录音是"市民帮他采数据"，从没说他的使命是"教市民怎么采数据"——角色与动作都被偷换。 
 D) 原词陷阱 To classify the flooding data processed 借了录音 processing that information 里的"处理数据"概念，但录音从没说使命是"给处理过的洪水数据分类"，classify 是凭空添加的动作。

questions.prompt: What did Loftis and his colleagues do to obtain data about water height and movement?
options: They set up Internet-connected water-level sensors.
They tracked the rising tides with video-cameras.
They used newly-developed supercomputing facilities.
They observed the direction of water flow on the spot.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did Loftis and his colleagues do to obtain data about water height and movement? 

 【翻译】 Loftis和他的同事们做了什么来获取有关水位高度和水流运动的数据? 
 A)  他们安装了联网的水位传感器。 
 B)  他们用摄像机追踪涨潮情况。 
 C)  他们使用了新开发的超级计算设施。 
 D)  他们现场观察水流方向。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They set up Internet-connected water-level sensors. 
 【定位】 P1 So, in 2017, Loftis and colleagues set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors throughout the flood risk community of Norfolk, Virginia. The new sensors relayed rough measurements about water height and movement to a computer at the Virginia Institute. 
 于是，2017 年，Loftis 和同事们在弗吉尼亚州诺福克的涝灾社区各处架设了一组共 28 个联网水位传感器。这些新传感器把关于水位高度和水流移动的粗略测量数据传回弗吉尼亚研究所的一台计算机。 

 【信号】 set up sensors + 紧跟 water height and movement 。答案句信号是动作动词 set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors，紧接着下一句出现题干的对象词 water height and movement，两句锁死"靠装传感器拿水位数据"。 

 【替换】 set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors ↔ They set up Internet-connected water-level sensors 略去数量，核心动作器材全留 

 【排除】 B) 偷换概念 They tracked the rising tides with video-cameras 看似对应录音 take photos of rising tides，但那是"市民用（手机）拍照"，不是"用 video-cameras 追踪"，且这是采图片、不是题干问的"水位与水流"数据，器材和数据类型都被换。 
 C) 原词陷阱 They used newly-developed supercomputing facilities 借了录音 supercomputing had advanced，但录音说超算是用来"整合天气预报模型"的背景能力，不是他们获取水位数据的手段，原词被搬错了位置。 
 D) 未提及 They observed the direction of water flow on the spot 说他们"实地观察水流方向"，录音获取水流靠的是传感器测量，从没说"实地肉眼观察方向"，属添加动作。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say has become something of a ritual?
options: To argue about the value of a college degree.
To debate the validity of current survey data.
To account for the drastic decline in employment among men.
To compare men without college degrees with those who have.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say has become something of a ritual? 

 【翻译】 说话者说什么已经成为一种惯例? 
 A)  争论大学学位的价值。 
 B)  辩论当前调查数据的有效性。 
 C)  解释男性就业急剧下降的原因。 
 D)  将没有大学学位的男性与有大学学位的男性进行比较。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） To argue about the value of a college degree. 
 【定位】 P1 Now, it's become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree, but as Current Population Survey data show, there has been a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees compared with those who have them. 
 如今，争论大学学历的价值已经几乎成了一种惯例，但正如"当前人口调查"的数据所显示的，没有大学学历的男性其就业出现了急剧下降，与有学历的人相比尤其如此。 

 【信号】 标志词 ritual 紧跟其定义 。答案句里 it's become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree 中 ritual 后面紧接的 to debate… 就是"惯例"的具体内容，标志词后面紧跟的不定式就是要听的落点。 

 【替换】 ritual to debate the value of a college degree ↔ To argue about the value of a college degree. debate 同义替换为 argue about 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音里确有 Current Population Survey data show，B 项 To debate the validity of current survey data. 借走 survey、data 让你"听到就想选"，但原文是"数据显示"，并非"争论数据是否可信"，答非所问。  借用原文：Current Population Survey data show 

 C) 张冠李戴 C 项 To account for the drastic decline in employment among men. 搬来了答案句后半的 a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees，但"成为惯例的"是前半句"争论学历价值"，"解释就业下降"是全篇要做的事、不是被称作 ritual 的那件事，张冠李戴。  借用原文：a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 项 To compare men without college degrees with those who have. 用了 men without college degrees compared with those who have them 的字眼，但 compared 在原文只是描述"下降"的对照背景，说话人意图并非"做对比"这件事本身，过度解读。  借用原文：men without college degrees compared with those who have them

questions.prompt: What did the researchers of a recent working paper consider first?
options: The increase in women taking up jobs.
The issue of changing job requirements.
The factor of wages.
The impact of inflation.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the researchers of a recent working paper consider first? 

 【翻译】 最近一篇工作论文的研究人员首先考虑了什么? 
 A)  女性从事工作的增加。 
 B)  工作要求变化的问题。 
 C)  工资因素。 
 D)  通货膨胀的影响。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） The factor of wages. 
 【定位】 P3 Let's look at that paper now. First, the researchers considered the issue of wages. 
 现在我们来看这篇论文。首先，研究者们考虑了工资这一问题。 

 【信号】 次序信号词 First 直接领出答案 。First, the researchers considered the issue of wages. 里 First 就是"最先考虑"的信号，它后面紧跟的 the issue of wages 即答案落点。 

 【替换】 the researchers considered the issue of wages ↔ The factor of wages. the issue of wages 概括为 The factor of wages 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 项 The increase in women taking up jobs. 对应录音 the increase in women participating in the workforce，但那是第 5 段"新增解释"里的内容，不是"首先考虑"的，答非所问。  借用原文：the increase in women participating in the workforce 

 B) 原词陷阱 B 项 The issue of changing job requirements. 指向 more jobs require a college degree today than in the past，但录音明说这是 the second theory，不是"首先"考虑的，次序错位。  借用原文：This leads to the second theory, that more jobs require a college degree today 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 项 The impact of inflation. 借走录音 adjusting for inflation 里的 inflation，但 inflation 在原文只是"调整通胀后"的限定语，研究者首先考虑的是 wages，不是通胀，原词陷阱。  借用原文：adjusting for inflation

questions.prompt: What did the recent paper identify as a new potential explanation of the problem concerning men's employment?
options: Men's unwillingness to accept low wages in times of growing inflation.
The wage gap between those with college degrees and those without.
More jobs requiring their holders to have a college degree nowadays.
The sharp decline in marriage among men with no college degrees.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the recent paper identify as a new potential explanation of the problem concerning men's employment? 

 【翻译】 最近的论文指出了关于男性就业问题的哪个新的潜在解释? 
 A)  男性在通货膨胀加剧时期不愿接受低工资。 
 B)  有大学学位者与无大学学位者之间的工资差距。 
 C)  如今更多工作要求持有者拥有大学学位。 
 D)  没有大学学位的男性结婚率急剧下降。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The sharp decline in marriage among men with no college degrees. 
 【定位】 P5 They identified two new potential explanations: the first being the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees since the 1960s; and the second being the increase in women participating in the workforce that was concurrent with the decline in marriage. 
 他们指出了两个新的可能解释：第一个是自上世纪六十年代以来，没有大学学历的男性婚姻率的剧烈下降；第二个是与婚姻下降同时出现的女性进入劳动力市场的增加。 

 【信号】 信号词 new、identified 领出两个新解释 。They identified two new potential explanations 里 new、identified 就是"新提出"的信号，冒号后的 the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees 即新解释之一。 

 【替换】 the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees ↔ The sharp decline in marriage among men with no college degrees. tremendous=sharp、without=with no 同义替换 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 项 Men's unwillingness to accept low wages in times of growing inflation. 拼接了 why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages 与 inflation，但这是第一个旧理论的内容，不是"新"解释，且原文说工资经通胀调整后"变化不大"，并非"通胀加剧"，既答非所问又与原文相反。  借用原文：why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages 

 B) 原词陷阱 B 项 The wage gap between those with college degrees and those without. 几乎照抄录音 the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without，但那是第 3 段已有的工资理论，不是第 5 段"新提出"的，原词陷阱。  借用原文：As the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 项 More jobs requiring their holders to have a college degree nowadays. 对应 more jobs require a college degree today than in the past，但这是 the second theory（旧理论），不在"new potential explanations"之列，答非所问。  借用原文：more jobs require a college degree today than in the past

questions.prompt: What has a market research team found in its latest fashion and sustainability report?
options: More and more people attach importance to protecting endangered animals.
More and more people prioritize animal welfare when buying things to wear.
An increasing number of people demand to free animals being kept in cages.
An increasing number of people follow the latest trend of becoming vegetarians.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What has a market research team found in its latest fashion and sustainability report? 

 【翻译】 一个市场研究团队在其最新的时尚与可持续性报告中发现了什么? 
 A)  越来越多的人重视保护濒危动物。 
 B)  越来越多的人在购买穿戴物品时优先考虑动物福利。 
 C)  越来越多的人要求释放被关在笼子里的动物。 
 D)  越来越多的人追随成为素食主义者的最新潮流。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） More and more people prioritize animal welfare when buying things to wear. 
 【定位】 P1 It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes, with 42% saying it was important to them. 
 调查发现，在人们买衣服前会考虑的诸多问题中，动物福利排在首位，有 42% 的人表示这点对他们很重要。 

 【信号】 主体 It found 直接领出发现 。录音用 It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes 把调查主体的「发现」直接端出来，「It found」就是答案句的信号——题目问发现什么，跟着 found 后面那句走即可。 

 【替换】 animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes ↔ prioritize animal welfare when buying things to wear came top=prioritize、buying clothes=things to wear 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 录音通篇讲 animal welfare(动物福利)和 animal-free(无动物成分)产品，从没说 protecting endangered animals(保护濒危动物)，A 把「动物福利」偷换成「濒危动物保护」，是听到 animal 就想选的诱饵。 
 C) 未提及 录音只字未提 free animals being kept in cages(放生笼中动物)，这是凭「动物」话题联想出来的内容，原文无据。 
 D) 原词陷阱 录音开头确有 an increasing number of people are trying to eat less meat，但那只是引出话题的背景，不是调查「发现」的内容；D becoming vegetarians 盗用了开头的「吃肉/吃素」原词来答非所问。  借用原文：While an increasing number of people are trying to eat less meat

questions.prompt: What have some world-renowned fashion designers done for some time?
options: Avoided the use of leather and fur.
Labelled all their products as vegan.
Refrained from using chemicals in their products.
Utilized a silk substitute made from mushrooms.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What have some world-renowned fashion designers done for some time? 

 【翻译】 一些世界知名的时装设计师一段时间以来做了什么? 
 A)  避免使用皮革和毛皮。 
 B)  将他们所有的产品标注为纯素产品。 
 C)  避免在产品中使用化学物质。 
 D)  使用由蘑菇制成的丝绸替代品。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Avoided the use of leather and fur. 
 【定位】 P2 At the top end, some of the world-renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time. 
 在高端领域，一些世界知名的时装设计师已经有一段时间不用皮革和皮草了。 

 【信号】 主体词+for some time 原样复现 。录音 some of the world-renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time 把题干的主体词和 for some time 几乎原样念出，这种「题干主体词在原文复现」就是答案句信号，紧跟其后的动词 avoided 即所做之事。 

 【替换】 have avoided leather and fur for some time ↔ Avoided the use of leather and fur. 近乎原词、仅补 the use of 

 【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 录音里 vegan 标签是 products registered with the vegan trademark、由 The Animal Free Product Society 与 New Look 等做的，不是高端设计师；B Labelled all their products as vegan. 把别人做的事安到设计师头上，且加了原文没有的 all。  借用原文：products registered with the vegan trademark 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音提到 the chemicals used for finishing them 是说做 vegan 产品要检查的环节，并未说设计师「拒用化学品」；C Refrained from using chemicals in their products. 盗用 chemicals 原词却编造了「拒用」这个原文没有的动作。  借用原文：the chemicals used for finishing them 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音说 some of the companies are now exploring a leather substitute and a silk replacement made from mushrooms，主体是 some companies、动作是 now exploring(正在探索)，既非「设计师长期所做」也非已经 utilized；D Utilized a silk substitute made from mushrooms. 盗用了 mushrooms 这个抢眼原词，但主体和时态都错位。  借用原文：some of the companies are now exploring a leather substitute and a silk replacement made from mushrooms

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say is unclear concerning vegan products?
options: Whether they actually signify a substantial change.
Whether they effectively protect animals at large.
Whether they can be considered sustainable.
Whether they can be regarded as ethical.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say is unclear concerning vegan products? 

 【翻译】 说话者说关于纯素产品有什么是不明确的? 
 A)  它们是否真正标志着实质性的改变。 
 B)  它们是否能有效地保护整体上的动物。 
 C)  它们是否可以被认为是可持续的。 
 D)  它们是否可以被视为符合伦理的。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Whether they can be regarded as ethical. 
 【定位】 P4 However, it is unclear whether these new products can be considered ethical. 
 然而，这些新产品是否能被视为合乎道德/伦理，尚不明确。 

 【信号】 However 转折后接 unclear 。录音先说 This signifies a change，紧接 However, it is unclear whether these new products can be considered ethical——转折词 However 加存疑词 unclear 双重信号叠加，转折之后才是真意，存疑的对象 ethical 就在这句里。 

 【替换】 whether these new products can be considered ethical ↔ Whether they can be regarded as ethical. considered=regarded as 同义 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音说 This signifies a change——「这标志着一种改变」是肯定语气、已成定论，恰恰不是 unclear 的对象；A a substantial change 盗用了 change 原词，却把已确定的事说成尚不明确，正话反说。  借用原文：This signifies a change 

 B) 答非所问 录音整体讲 animal-free/animal welfare，但说 unclear 的那句问的是 ethical，不是 protect animals at large；B 借了全篇的「动物」话题来冒充存疑对象，原文没把「是否真护动物」列为不明确之事。 
 C) 原词陷阱 录音只在开头报告名 fashion and sustainability report 出现过 sustainability，从未说「是否可持续」尚不明确；C sustainable 盗用了这个开头出现的原词来答非所问。  借用原文：fashion and sustainability report

questions.prompt: What is one of the facts stated by the speaker?
options: The era we live in is the most peaceful in history.
The world has seen more violence in recent years.
The environmental welfare has worsened in the world.
The belief is less prevalent that the world is going to hell.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is one of the facts stated by the speaker? 

 【翻译】 说话者陈述的事实之一是什么? 
 A)  我们生活的时代是历史上最和平的。 
 B)  近年来世界上发生了更多暴力事件。 
 C)  世界环境福祉已经恶化。 
 D)  认为世界正在走向毁灭的观念不那么普遍了。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） The era we live in is the most peaceful in history. 
 【定位】 P2 We are living in history's most peaceful era, with violence of all kinds in steep decline. Those are the facts. 
 我们正生活在历史上最和平的时代，各类暴力都在急剧下降。这些就是事实。 

 【信号】 'Those are the facts' 直接点明这是事实 。演讲者紧接着用 Those are the facts. 给前面一串陈述盖章为'事实'，这就是答案信号；其中 history's most peaceful era 正对应题干要的那个 fact。 

 【替换】 history's most peaceful era ↔ the most peaceful in history 同义改写：词序调换、词性微调 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 选项说 more violence in recent years，但录音明说 violence of all kinds in steep decline（各类暴力急剧下降），方向正好相反，是把'下降'听反成'增多'。  借用原文：violence of all kinds in steep decline 

 C) 与原文相反 选项称 environmental welfare has worsened，但录音说每一项 environmental welfare…has improved rather than deteriorated（改善而非恶化），用 worsened 偷换了 improved，方向反了。  借用原文：Every single measure of material and environmental welfare…has improved rather than deteriorated 

 D) 未提及 选项说'认为世界要完蛋的信念不那么流行了'，但录音恰恰描述这种悲观信念很普遍（everything was terrible, and that the world was going to hell、第 3 段多数英法人觉得世界在变坏），从没说它在减弱，属凭空生造。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about most British and French people in a 2015 survey for YouGov?
options: They were actually not in their right mind.
They believed the world was deteriorating.
They did not wish to live in the previous century.
They were convinced by the statistics presented to them.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about most British and French people in a 2015 survey for YouGov? 

 【翻译】 关于2015年YouGov调查中的大多数英国人和法国人,我们了解到什么? 
 A)  他们实际上神智不清。 
 B)  他们认为世界正在恶化。 
 C)  他们不愿生活在上个世纪。 
 D)  他们被呈现给他们的统计数据说服了。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They believed the world was deteriorating. 
 【定位】 P3 In a 2015 survey for YouGov, 65% of British people and 81% of the French said they thought the world was getting worse. 
 在 2015 年一项 YouGov 的调查中，65% 的英国人和 81% 的法国人说他们认为世界正在变糟。 

 【信号】 专名 YouGov/2015 直接领出答案句 。题干的专名锚点 In a 2015 survey for YouGov 在原文原样出现，紧跟其后的 said they thought the world was getting worse 就是这群人的看法，即答案信号。 

 【替换】 the world was getting worse ↔ the world was deteriorating 同义改写：getting worse = deteriorating 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 选项说这群人 not in their right mind，原文确有 Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century，但这是演讲者自己的评论，不是调查显示这群人神志不清；把演讲者的话安到调查对象头上。  借用原文：Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century. 

 C) 张冠李戴 选项 did not wish to live in the previous century 同样取自 Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century，但这仍是演讲者的论断，且原文是说'没人该希望活在过去'，并非调查里这群人表达了此意愿。  借用原文：Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century. 

 D) 与原文相反 选项说他们 convinced by the statistics presented to them，但原文说按 numerous sensible statistics, these people are simply wrong——统计数据恰恰证明他们错了，他们并未被数据说服，方向相反。  借用原文：according to numerous sensible statistics, these people are simply wrong

questions.prompt: What does our prevailing mood of despair indicate?
options: The subjectivity of mass media.
The current state of affairs.
Our psychological biases.
Our ancestors' influence.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does our prevailing mood of despair indicate? 

 【翻译】 我们普遍存在的绝望情绪表明了什么? 
 A)  大众媒体的主观性。 
 B)  当前的事态。 
 C)  我们的心理偏见。 
 D)  我们祖先的影响。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Our psychological biases. 
 【定位】 P4 It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors—but now, in a media-saturated era, constantly mislead us. 
 它最好被解释为种种心理偏见的结果——这些偏见曾对我们的进化祖先有用，但如今在一个被媒体充斥的时代，却不断误导我们。 

 【信号】 归因信号 'explained as the result of' 。演讲者用 It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases 明确把这股绝望情绪归因到'心理偏见'，explained as the result of 就是答案信号，其后名词即题目要的答案。 

 【替换】 various psychological biases ↔ Our psychological biases. 近乎原词，仅限定词不同 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 选项说 The subjectivity of mass media.，原文虽提到 in a media-saturated era（媒体充斥的时代），但那只是偏见'被放大'的背景，演讲者归因的根源是心理偏见，而非'媒体的主观性'，把背景偷换成根源。  借用原文：in a media-saturated era, constantly mislead us 

 B) 与原文相反 选项说反映 The current state of affairs.，但原文明说这情绪 says more about us than it does about how things really are——它说的是我们自己，而非事情的真实状况，正好相反。  借用原文：It says more about us than it does about how things really are. 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项 Our ancestors' influence. 盗用原文 served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors 里的 ancestors，听到这个词很想选；但原文是说偏见曾对祖先有用，演讲者把绝望情绪直接归因到'心理偏见'本身，而非'祖先的影响'。  借用原文：that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors

questions.prompt: What was a very good thing in our evolutionary past?
options: Spreading exciting news around us far and wide.
Vacuuming up depressing or enraging stories.
Calculating dangerous risks to our survival.
Paying attention to negative information.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What was a very good thing in our evolutionary past? 

 【翻译】 在我们的进化历史中什么是非常好的事情? 
 A)  把令人兴奋的消息广泛传播到我们周围。 
 B)  大量吸收令人沮丧或愤怒的故事。 
 C)  计算对我们生存的危险风险。 
 D)  关注负面信息。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Paying attention to negative information. 
 【定位】 P5 In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival. 
 在我们的进化过去，注意力容易被负面信息攫取是一件很好的事，因为这很可能意味着对我们自身生存的危险威胁。 

 【信号】 原句直给 'a very good thing that…' 。题干 a very good thing 在原文原样出现于 it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information，that 从句里的内容就是那件'好事'，即答案信号。 

 【替换】 our attention could be easily seized by negative information ↔ Paying attention to negative information. 被动转主动 + 概括：被攫取注意 = 关注负面信息 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 选项说 Spreading exciting news around us far and wide.，但原文说 Really good news…can be a lot harder to spot（好消息其实更难被注意到），且演讲者夸的是关注'坏'消息有生存价值，不是传播好消息，方向相反。  借用原文：Really good news…can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper
